title: Consolidated Evidence Pack Generator + Priority-Lane Routing for Enterprise Security Intake
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Build an automated 'Evidence Pack Generator' that compiles the set of artifacts (policies, logs, config snapshots, audit trails, certification PDFs) required by SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR questionnaire responses and a parallel priority-lane router that assigns incoming security/compliance requests into triage lanes (Self-serve, Concierge, Legal Review, Enterprise SLA) based on risk signals and contractual context.

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to provide contract-required evidence and answers from days to hours for standard asks.
- Make routing deterministic and auditable so SLA commitments are measurable and enforceable.
- Surface minimal competencies for Concierge lane (human ops) and automatic fallbacks when evidence is stale.

Scope in this ticket:
- Define schema for an Evidence Pack (manifest of artifacts with provenance metadata).
- Implement prototype pack generation using available S3/Drive sources + Confluence templates.
- Risk scoring rules for lane assignment (region/data classification, requested controls, contract tier, product deployment type: hosted/dedicated/private).
- Integration glue: intake form -> prioritization service -> evidence pack builder -> response template creator -> dispatch to Zendesk/CS.

Acceptance criteria:
- PoC evidence pack created for 3 common ask types (SOC2 control list, GDPR DPA checklist, HIPAA logging evidence) with provenance links.
- Routing assigns >90% of test sample tickets into correct lane according to rubric.
- Dashboard widget in Console shows queue sizes and average time-to-response by lane.
- Hand-off docs for Concierge ops and Legal with checklist and escalation paths.

Proposed solution components and trade-offs:
1) Evidence manifest (lightweight JSON/YAML) that lists artifacts + canonical source + last-updated timestamp. Trade-off: keep manifest minimal vs fully normalize artifact types (we start minimal to ship quickly).
2) Pack builder service that pulls artifacts from Drive/Confluence/S3 and zips them with index.html. Trade-off: building connectors for every storage system now increases scope; initial release will support Drive + Confluence + S3, with a generic webhook-based connector for others.
3) Priority-lane router based on rule engine (configurable by PM/Security). Trade-off: Rule engine allows fast iteration but risks inconsistencies; alternative ML-based scoring deferred to later cycle.
4) Governance: pack expiration TTL and automated 'stale' alerts. Trade-off: shorter TTL increases churn but improves accuracy.

Open questions:
- Should evidence packs be stored in customer-specific buckets or ephemeral on request? (Security/Legal prefers ephemeral with audit trail).
- Which vendor questionnaire formats do we prioritize (SIG, BBP, custom)?
- Do we expose pack generation API to dedicated/private customers or restrict to Hosted?
